```{r setup, include = FALSE}
# Auth/network chunks are shown but not run at build time; the chunks on an
# in-memory frame below run, so their output is real.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

Follow delivery error rates by carrier, day by day and cumulatively, across every ongoing campaign -- with T-Mobile's 4780 volume rejection split out -- from the **live delivery metrics**. Assumes you have completed First-time setup (the package README, or `?s160_gcs_init` from R): Cloud Storage access to `s160_analytics_prod`.

## Pull a range of days

The live metrics are one file per ET day, starting 2026-09-29. Each run of the pipeline (currently 4pm and 9pm ET) rewrites today's and yesterday's files. Pull the days you want, then roll them up:

```{r}
library(survey160r)
s160_gcs_init()   # one browser sign-in, cached

paths <- live_metrics_pull(date_from = "2026-10-01")   # through today (ET); finished days cached
rates <- live_metrics_error_rates(paths)               # one row per carrier and day
```

`date_to` defaults to today (ET), and `date_from` to 30 days before it. The result is a named vector of local paths, one per day that has a file; `live_metrics_pull()` messages how many it downloaded and which days had no file.

## Error rates by carrier

`live_metrics_error_rates()` defaults to `by = "carrier"`. On a frame it does no I/O, so this runs:

```{r carrier, eval = TRUE}
library(survey160r)
cells <- data.frame(
  et_date = as.Date(rep(c("2026-11-01", "2026-11-02"), each = 4)),
  et_hour = 10L, brand = "B1", campaign_id = 1234L,
  carrier = rep(c("T-Mobile", "T-Mobile", "Verizon", "Verizon"), 2),
  error_code = rep(c("(none)", "4780", "(none)", "4700"), 2),
  n_sent = c(90L, 10L, 195L, 5L, 70L, 30L, 196L, 4L),
  n_engaged = 0L
)
rates <- live_metrics_error_rates(cells)
rates[, c("et_date", "carrier", "n_sent", "n_error", "error_rate", "cum_error_rate")]
```

T-Mobile's day rate jumps from 10% to 30% on the second day, while its cumulative rate (both days together) reads 20%. With real data, `cells` is `paths` from the pull.

## Across the whole fleet

`by = NULL` gives one row per day for every carrier together:

```{r fleet, eval = TRUE}
live_metrics_error_rates(cells, by = NULL)[, c("et_date", "n_sent", "error_rate", "cum_error_rate")]
```

## By brand or campaign

`by` takes any of `"carrier"`, `"brand"`, `"campaign_id"`, `"error_code"` and `"et_hour"`, alone or together. `campaign_ids` scopes the rollup to a set of campaigns:

```{r}
live_metrics_error_rates(paths, by = "brand")
live_metrics_error_rates(paths, by = c("carrier", "brand"))
live_metrics_error_rates(paths, by = "carrier", campaign_ids = c(1234, 1235))
live_metrics_error_rates(paths, by = "error_code")   # which codes make up the errors
```

## Follow T-Mobile 4780

Each code in `codes` (default `"4780"`) gets its own `n_<code>`, `rate_<code>`, `cum_<code>` and `cum_rate_<code>`, so the volume rejection can be read apart from the other errors:

```{r tmobile, eval = TRUE}
tmobile <- subset(rates, carrier == "T-Mobile")
tmobile[, c("et_date", "n_sent", "n_4780", "rate_4780", "cum_4780", "cum_rate_4780")]
```

Add codes to split out more of them, e.g. `codes = c("4780", "4700")`; `codes = character(0)` adds none. `percent = TRUE` scales every rate to `0`-`100`.

## Find the day a block started

Read the daily rate, not the cumulative one: keep the days a carrier's code rate crosses a threshold you choose, and the first of them is the onset:

```{r onset, eval = TRUE}
subset(rates, rate_4780 >= 0.2)[, c("et_date", "carrier", "n_sent", "rate_4780")]
```

To narrow it to the hour, break the day down by `et_hour` and read the daily columns (with `et_hour` in `by`, the running totals run per hour across days, which is rarely what you want):

```{r}
live_metrics_error_rates(paths, by = c("carrier", "et_hour"),
                         date_from = "2026-11-02", date_to = "2026-11-02")
```

`et_hour` is the ET hour of each recipient's first send, not the hour the rejection came back.

## Daily or cumulative

- **Daily** (`n_sent`, `n_error`, `error_rate`) -- the recipients first sent that day. Use it to spot the day a carrier starts rejecting.
- **Cumulative** (`cum_sent`, `cum_error`, `cum_error_rate`) -- every recipient first sent from the group's first day pulled through that day (a carrier that first appears later starts its total there). Use it for the running picture; it moves slowly, so a one-day spike barely shows.

The cumulative columns start at the first day in what you pass in. To start the running total at a given day, pass `date_from` (and `date_to` to end it):

```{r}
live_metrics_error_rates(paths, date_from = "2026-10-15")
```

## Plot a cumulative rate

ggplot2 is not a survey160r dependency; with it installed:

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(rates, aes(et_date, cum_error_rate, colour = carrier)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(x = "ET day", y = "Cumulative delivery error rate", colour = NULL)
```

Base graphics need nothing extra, one line per carrier:

```{r}
tmobile <- subset(rates, carrier == "T-Mobile")
plot(tmobile$et_date, tmobile$cum_error_rate, type = "l",
     xlab = "ET day", ylab = "Cumulative error rate", main = "T-Mobile")
lines(tmobile$et_date, tmobile$cum_rate_4780, lty = 2)   # the 4780 share
```

## What you get back

`live_metrics_error_rates()` returns one row per `by` group and ET day, sorted by `by` then `et_date`:

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `et_date` | The ET day. |
| the `by` columns | The group, e.g. `carrier`; none with `by = NULL`. |
| `n_sent` / `n_error` | Recipients first sent that day, and those whose latest delivery code is an error. |
| `error_rate` | `n_error / n_sent`. |
| `cum_sent` / `cum_error` | The same counts summed from the group's first day in `x` through `et_date`. |
| `cum_error_rate` | `cum_error / cum_sent`. |
| `n_4780` / `rate_4780` / `cum_4780` / `cum_rate_4780` | One set per code in `codes`: its count, its daily rate, its running count, and its cumulative rate. |

A rate with no sends is `NA`. `live_metrics_records()` returns the cells -- `et_date`, `et_hour`, `carrier`, `brand`, `campaign_id`, `error_code` (`"(none)"` = no error) and the `n_sent` / `n_engaged` counts -- for your own slicing. See `?live_metrics_records` and `?live_metrics_error_rates`.

## Notes

- **Counts are per recipient, not per message.** Each recipient is counted once per campaign, on the day and hour of their *first* send, under their *latest* delivery code as of the day's last rewrite (9pm ET the next day). A rejection that a retry delivered by then no longer counts as an error, a code that changes after it is not picked up, and a recipient sent on several days counts once, on the first. A phone in two campaigns counts in each, so a fleet-wide rollup counts it twice. Because a retried rejection drops out, the error rates are a floor, not the share of messages rejected.
- **Recent days still move.** Today's and yesterday's files are rewritten on each run with the latest delivery codes, so read the last two days as provisional. Today has no file until the day's first run (4pm ET), so a pull before then reports no file for today.
- **Caching.** A day is final at 03:00 ET two days after it (Nov 1 at 03:00 ET on Nov 3, after its last rewrite at 9pm ET on Nov 2); a cached copy downloaded after that is reused without a network call. Any other copy (today, yesterday, the day before until 03:00 ET, or a day you cached before it was final) is fetched again on every pull. `refresh = TRUE` re-downloads the whole range.
- **Missing days.** A day with no file (before 2026-09-29, or not yet written) is skipped with a message; a day with no sends has a file with no rows. Neither gives the day a row in the rates (not a row with `n_sent = 0`), and the running totals continue across the gap.
- **Coverage.** A file covers the campaigns in the live phone lists when it was written; a campaign archived before its day's last rewrite is missing from that day.
- **Unknown carrier or brand.** The files write a missing carrier or brand as `"(unknown)"`; the readers turn it into `NA`, which groups as its own row, as in `disposition_funnel()`. Filter it with `is.na()`.
- **Aggregate, not phone-keyed.** The files hold counts, never phone numbers. To screen a sample on past delivery errors, see `vignette("disposition")`.
- **`env`.** `live_metrics_pull()` reads `"prod"` (default) or `"dev"` -- there is no `staging` tier, so `env = "staging"` errors. Only prod runs on a schedule; dev has a file only for the days its job was run by hand, so a dev pull mostly reports days with no file. Run `s160_datasets()` to see every dataset's environments.
